answer.text: Earning exempt income (e.g., tax-free dividends historically)

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 14A of the Income-tax Act, expenditure incurred in relation to income that does not form part of total income (i.e., exempt income) is disallowed when computing taxable income. The logic is that a taxpayer cannot earn tax-free income and also claim a tax deduction for the costs of earning it. The Trap: General business expenses, capital gains, and salary income are not the targets of Section 14A — those are computed under their own heads. Section 14A specifically addresses expenses tied to exempt income. Note: Section 14A is a provision of the Income-tax Act and the specific Section 14A disallowance rule was not located in the cited NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook pages (the assigned tax chapter pages discuss residency, capital gains, dividends, interest income, business income, buybacks, and Section 9A). The framing above is general direct-tax law rather than a direct workbook citation.
